author: Nicholas Fogleman
title: Douglas County's free rideshare service launches in Parker - NewsBreak
text:
By Nicholas Fogleman ,
4 hours ago Officials gathered to celebrate the expansion of the county's free rideshare service, Link on Demand April 8,2026. (Courtesy pf Link on Demand) Douglas County’s free rideshare service, Link on Demand, has formally launched in the town of Parker.
Officials gathered Thursday to mark the expansion, which will bring free, door-to-door rides to residents in eastern Douglas County.
“This innovative free rideshare service is more than just a new transportation option. It’s a meaningful investment in our citizenry and the future of Parker. It makes it easier for people to get to work, access important services, and stay connected with one another,” Parker Mayor Joshua Rivero said.
The service began in 2014 as a fixed route transit service in Lone Tree. It has since expanded to Highlands Ranch and evolved into a door-to-door, app-based transit system providing over 160,000 rides annually.
County commissioners in February approved a $4.4 million contract to continue existing services and expand east into Stonegate and Parker. The expansion is expected to cost $1.2 million, with the town contributing $250,000.
The Via-operated service is designed to serve a wide range of riders, including older adults, individuals with disabilities and residents without access to a personal vehicle, though anyone within the service area may request a ride. Wheelchair accessible vehicles and other accommodations are available upon request.
“It is about senior citizens that are homebound that don’t necessarily have access to rides, or maybe that they don’t have a license anymore, but they have to get to those doctor’s appointments,” Laydon said. “It’s a great opportunity for homes that just have a single vehicle.”
Officials said the program has seen significant growth. In Highlands Ranch, where Link on Demand officially launched in May 2025, the service has delivered more than 72,000 trips, and in Lone Tree, a record 73,000 rides were provided last year.
County Commissioner Abe Laydon acknowledged the county’s investment in the service.
“These are the tax dollars coming from the people, but it pays for itself because people are going, according to the data, to Walmart, King Soopers, Park Meadows Mall, hopefully Castle Rock Outlet soon, and downtown Parker,” Laydon said. “That’s how we get revenues through sales tax.”
County officials said the long-term goal is to continue expanding Link on Demand throughout Douglas County.
“The vision is for Link on Demand to be throughout the entire county,” Laydon said. “Anywhere you need to go within the County of Douglas would be accessible.”
More information about the service, including service areas and how to request a ride, is available on Douglas County’s Link on Demand website .
